prompt.context: Due to recent downturn in the Brazilian economy, BizAvi Company is currently seeking to diversify its portfolio of products and improve profitability. The Maintenance BU currently supports third party clients and the company's owned business jets, which are operated by the Aircraft Chartering Unit. BizAvi Company has recently acquired three new units of Embraer aircraft, and currently outsources the maintenance services to the manufacturer. The CEO sees in the Embraer models also an opportunity for the Maintenance Business Unit, and has asked your help to assess the quality of this project.
prompt.question: Should BizAvi Company insource the maintenance of its Embraer aircraft (and potentially offer this service to third-party clients)? Assess the viability of this project.

clarifying_info.a: The company operates in Brazil, and most of its clients are also Brazilian.

clarifying_info.q: What does the maintenance service include?
clarifying_info.a: It consists of providing technical support for preventive and corrective aircraft maintenance, including the supply of specialized labor and parts.

clarifying_info.q: What is the CEO's main objective?
clarifying_info.a: The main objective is to increase financial gain.

clarifying_info.q: Who currently services the Embraer aircraft?
clarifying_info.a: The Aircraft Chartering Unit currently outsources the service to the aircraft manufacturer's service center.

clarifying_info.q: How many Embraer aircraft does the company own?
clarifying_info.a: The company currently owns and operates three Embraer aircraft, with no plans to change the size of the fleet.

clarifying_info.q: How is BizAvi positioned in the market?
clarifying_info.a: BizAvi Company is a very renowned company in the country, and is well known for the technical expertise of its maintenance personnel.
The company has a VP for the Maintenance BU and a VP for the Air Chartering Unit.

clarifying_info.q: What does a repair station certification require?
clarifying_info.a: A repair station holds a licence to work on a list of determined aircraft models. This list depends on having appropriate resources: trained labor, specialized equipment and technical publications.

exhibits.title: BizAvi Company Portfolio
exhibits.shows: A table comparing the four aircraft models (Embraer, Model 1, Model 2, Model 3) across: manhours per aircraft (HH/aircraft), price per manhour ($/HH), cost of goods sold (COGS in $), markup on parts, days in hangar, hangar spots used, total market size, and current market share. The Embraer row is marked as not yet included in the portfolio.

exhibits.title: Embraer Aircraft - Maintenance Market in Brazil
exhibits.shows: A table listing four service providers (Embraer Service Center, Service Center 1, Service Center 2, Service Center 3) with their price per hour and markup on parts, plus a pie chart showing Embraer models market share by provider. Each aircraft uses on average 400 HH per year.

data.note: Each aircraft uses on average 400 HH/year. Markup is how much to add to COGS to calculate the customer's final price.

framework: Strategy: Assess alignment with long-term vision; whether certification strengthens the Air Chartering BU; potential to service third-party Embraer aircraft; funding availability
Market: Attractiveness and size of the Embraer maintenance market in Brazil; BizAvi's competitive position vs. existing service centers
Financials: Required one-time investment; annual revenues; annual costs (labor, materials, other); profit; NPV vs. hurdle rate
Internal Capabilities: Current resources (labor, equipment, certifications); gaps and availability in the market
Risks and Alternatives: Operational risks (maintenance delays affecting Air Chartering revenues); strategic risks; risk allocation between BUs

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate and compare the Contribution Margin and Contribution Margin per hangar spot per day for the Embraer model vs. the existing portfolio models.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute CM = ($/HH * HH/aircraft) + (markup * COGS) for each model, then divide by (days in hangar * spots) to get CM/spot/day. Key insight: Embraer has the lowest CM/spot/day at $950, worse than all current models (Model 1: $1,200; Model 2: $1,500; Model 3: $2,250). Candidate should flag this but still consider that owning 3 Embraer aircraft makes insourcing worth exploring for cost savings and strategic reasons.

math.setup: CM = (price_per_HH * HH_per_aircraft) + (markup * COGS); CM_per_spot_per_day = CM / (days_in_hangar * spots)
math.answer: Embraer CM/spot/day = $950 — lowest in the portfolio. Adding this model will dilute the overall Maintenance BU gross margin percentage.

questions.prompt: Using the Investment Analysis data, calculate the annual revenues, annual costs (including required headcount), annual profit, and NPV of insourcing Embraer maintenance for the owned fleet of 3 aircraft.
questions.guidance: Candidate must determine headcount from total HH demand and productivity assumptions. Key steps: (1) total HH = 400*3 = 1,200; adjusted for 75% productivity = 1,600 HH needed; each employee delivers 40 weeks * 40 HH/week = 1,600 HH/year, so 1 employee needed. Revenue = (labor + parts) * 3 aircraft. NPV using perpetuity formula = annual profit / discount rate minus initial investment. Positive NPV of ~$188k signals project is financially viable. Payback is approximately 3-4 years.

math.setup: Revenues = (price_per_HH * 400 HH + parts_price) * 3 aircraft; Costs = COGS*3 + labor + other (10% of revenues); NPV = (annual profit / discount rate) - investment
steps: Headcount: total HH demand = 400*3 = 1,200 HH; adjusted for 75% productivity = 1,200/0.75 = 1,600 HH; hours per employee per year = 40 weeks * 40 HH = 1,600 HH; employees needed = 1,600/1,600 = 1 employee
math.answer: Annual profit ≈ $28,800; NPV ≈ $188,000; Payback ≈ 3-4 years. Project is financially attractive.

questions.prompt: (Optional / advanced) The VP of Air Chartering shared financial data on the Embraer models. Question 1: What is the revenue impact of a 2-day delay on the Air Chartering Unit? Question 2: What are the main reasons a maintenance job could be delayed?
questions.guidance: Q1: Candidate multiplies price per flight by gross margin by flights per day. Lost revenue = $10,000 * 50% margin * 2 hours/flight * (3 flights / 2 days) * 2 days. Result is $30,000 in lost contribution over 2 days — this risk dwarfs the annual Maintenance BU profit of ~$29k if delays are frequent. Q2: Candidate should brainstorm technical and non-technical reasons.

math.setup: Lost CM per day = price_per_hour * GM% * avg_flight_hours * flights_per_day; total for 2 days
steps: Flights per day = 3 flights / 2 days = 1.5 flights/day
math.answer: A 2-day delay costs the Air Chartering Unit approximately $30,000 in lost contribution margin — roughly equal to the entire annual profit from the Maintenance insourcing project.

brainstorming.prompt: What do you believe to be the client's main drivers when choosing a maintenance provider?

categories.name: Technical
ideas: Minimum aircraft downtime (speed and no delays)

categories.name: Non-Technical
ideas: Availability of technicians in emergency situations

recommendation: The project is financially attractive: expected NPV of approximately $188,000 and annual profit of ~$29,000 considering only the owned fleet of 3 aircraft
There is an upside opportunity to capture third-party Embraer clients in a 150-aircraft market where BizAvi currently has 0% share, which would significantly improve profits and NPV
The required investment is modest ($100,000 one-time) and payback is approximately 3-4 years, making this a low-risk financial commitment
Recommendation: proceed with insourcing Embraer maintenance
risks: A 2-day maintenance delay could cost the Air Chartering Unit ~$30,000 in lost contribution — nearly equal to one full year of Maintenance BU profit from this project; the company must ensure delivery reliability at least equal to the Embraer Service Center
Adding the Embraer model will dilute the Maintenance BU's overall gross margin percentage, as Embraer CM/spot/day ($950) is the lowest in the portfolio
Entering a market where Embraer Service Center holds 80% share will be challenging; price is not the primary driver, so BizAvi must compete on quality, availability and brand
Regulatory and certification requirements (repair station licence) must be met before commencing commercial services
next_steps: Obtain the repair station certification for Embraer aircraft models
Develop a marketing plan targeting third-party Embraer operators in Brazil
Establish strict SLA and contingency procedures to protect Air Chartering Unit revenue from maintenance delays
Monitor portfolio-level gross margin quarterly to assess the dilution effect of the new model
